asset.name: Quant

score_rationales.supply: QNT’s supply is capped at 14,612,493 tokens with no inflationary emissions (full mint at the 2018 TGE; circulating supply is ~14.54M per major aggregators, roughly 99.5% of max). Glassnode’s labeled exchange share is about 10.2% of supply (Mar 2026), indicating most tokens sit off exchanges though short-term trend was not verified here. Operational demand locks QNT as gateway/licensing collateral, which mechanically reduces tradeable float versus the fixed cap, while precise foundation and insider wallet concentration is harder to audit without full CoinGecko-style supply metadata.
score_rationales.wyckoff: Wyckoff phase carried from last snapshot until the next daily indicators refresh.
score_rationales.adoption_activity: Adoption is evidenced by large institutional programs—UK Finance selected R3 and Quant in April 2024 to deliver the UK Regulated Liability Network experimentation prototype (participants include Barclays, HSBC, Mastercard, Visa, etc.), Overledger underpinned Bank of England/BIS Project Rosalind retail CBDC work, and Quant provides interoperability gateways on IDB-backed LACChain across 12 Latin American and Caribbean countries—while public aggregate Overledger TPS, tx/day, or a global validator count are not published like an open L1, so measurable usage stays moderate.
score_rationales.value_capture: QNT’s max supply is fixed at about 14.61M with no ongoing mint (2018 TGE), and Overledger licensing and gateway collateral tie enterprise usage to treasury-held and locked QNT, which can tighten float but does not route cash flows to passive holders. Public materials emphasize fiat or QNT payment for licenses and lack a transparent, recurring fee-burn, buyback-to-holder, or inflation-offsetting staking yield comparable to fee-sharing DeFi or burn-heavy L1s, so holder accrual stays indirect versus category peers.
